correctness.finding: PASS. The tournament upper bound is valid: a transitive (r+1)-vertex subtournament orders a principal submatrix triangularly with nonzero diagonal, so every rank-r fooling-set matrix has fewer than 2^r rows. At r=3, equality n=7 forces a regular 7-tournament whose in-neighborhood triples form the unique Steiner triple system STS(7). Factoring M through F^3 converts those triples into seven projective-line incidences. Normalizing three noncollinear points reduces the final Fano incidence to determinant -2, so n=7 is possible only in characteristic two. I independently checked the submitted universal 6x6 matrix has rank three and a unit 3x3 minor over every field, and the 7x7 characteristic-two matrix satisfies the fooling-set condition and has rank three over F_2.

originality.finding: PASS, narrowly scoped. Dietzfelbinger–Hromkovič–Schnitger supply the classical quadratic rank bound; Klauck–de Wolf supply a size-six rank-three construction; Friesen–Hamed–Lee–Theis supply the characteristic-two size-seven instance as part of their positive-characteristic families. Those are prior art. Targeted literature and current-repository searches did not locate the exact rank-three extremal theorem, the characteristic-dependent 6-versus-7 classification, or the Fano-plane obstruction. The elementary general tournament bound itself is treated as a supporting lemma rather than the principal novelty claim.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. The result closes the first nontrivial exact low-rank case of the fooling-set-versus-rank problem, proves optimality of the two known rank-three constructions in their respective characteristic regimes, and explains the characteristic split through projective Fano incidence. It does not overclaim asymptotic improvement or classification of all extremizers.
